title: CDs by Ace Frehley, Mr. Bungle, and UFO are released in new versions in Brazil
excerpt: CDs by Ace Frehley, Mr. Bungle, and UFO are getting new editions in Brazil through a partnership between Wikimetal and Oporto da Música.
content:
New releases from Wikimetal Store. Credit: Press release.

3 hours ago

New releases are the result of a partnership between Wikimetal and Oporto da Música.

Through the Wikimetal with Oporto da Música, classic rock and metal albums that were difficult to find or had never even been released in Brazil are arriving monthly on the national market. The new editions of the titles in CD format, some with slipcases, are available in major stores and online via Wikimetal Store.

Ace Frehley

Frehley's Comet (1987) is the second solo project by the former Kiss guitarist and was the first released after his departure from the band. Formed in 1984, the original band consisted of Ace (lead guitar, lead and backing vocals), Richie Scarlet (rhythm and lead guitar, lead and backing vocals), John Regan (bass, backing vocals), Arthur Stead (keyboards), and Anton Fig (drums). The group recorded several demos and songs around 1984 and 1985, and many of them were performed live; however, the songs from that time remain officially unreleased, and only a few of them made it onto the final recording of Frehley's Comet .

Mr. Bungle

Mr. Bungle is the self-titled debut album by the experimental rock band. Released in 1991, the album features several genre shifts, characteristic of the group, which contributed to their increased popularity and solidified a loyal audience. Mr. Bungle blends a variety of musical styles, primarily funk metal, avant-rock, alternative metal, ska and avant-garde jazz, elements of avant-garde metal, circus music, heavy metal, free jazz and funk. The lyrics, in turn, address various themes, ranging from the comedic to the dark or sexual.

UFO

UFO 's seventh album , Obsession (1978), was the last to feature Michael Schenker on lead guitar, until his return to the band in 1993. The project was recorded in an abandoned post office in Los Angeles. The 2008 remastered edition includes three live bonus tracks.
